A = analog input                              All digital inputs are Schmitt trigger inputs, digital input
I = digital input signal                    and output levels are LVCMOS/LVTTL compatible. Port A
O = digital output signal                   Pins (PA0 - PA7) must not be driven above VDD_IO, all
PU = pull-up                                other digital inputs are 5 V tolerant. Pull-ups are
I/O = digital input/output signal           programmable for all GPIO pins.
N = not to be connected
P = power or ground                         Alternate Pin Functions
PD = pull-down                                GPIO Pins are shared with dedicated Input/Output signals

                                            of on-chip peripherals. The following table lists the
                                            available functions on each GPIO pin.

should not be assumed, damage may occur and reliability may be affected.

Note on current consumption in TX mode                               Table 5. CURRENT CONSUMPTION VS. OUTPUT
  To achieve best output power the matching network has to           POWER

be optimized for the desired output power and frequency. As                                          Itxcalc [mA]
a rule of thumb a good matching network produces about
50% efficiency with the AX8052F143 power amplifier                   Pout [dBm]             868 MHz                169 MHz
although over 90% are theoretically possible. A typical
matching network has between 1 dB and 2 dB loss (Ploss).             0                      7.5                    4.5
The theoretical efficiencies are the same for the single ended
PA (ANTP1) and differential PA (ANTP and ANTN)                       1                      7.9                    4.9
therefore only one current value is shown in the table below.
We recommend to use the single ended PA for low output               2                      8.4                    5.4
power and the differential PA for high power. The
differential PA is internally multiplexed with the LNA on            3                      9.0                    6.0
pins ANTP and ANTN. Therefore constraints for the RX
matching have to be considered for the differential PA               4                      9.8                    6.8
matching.

1. Tolerances and start-up times depend on the crystal used. Depending on the RF frequency and channel spacing the IC must be calibrated
    to the exact crystal frequency using the readings of the register AX5043_TRKFREQ.

2. The choice of crystal oscillator or TCXO frequency depends on the targeted regulatory regime for TX, see separate documentation on
    meeting regulatory requirements.

3. To avoid spurious emission, the crystal or TCXO reference frequency should be chosen so that the RF carrier frequency is not an integer
    multiple of the crystal or TCXO frequency.

4. The oscillator transconductance is regulated for fastest start-up time during start-up and for lowest power curing steady state oscillation.
    This means that values depend on the crystal used.

                                                                          9

                                                 AX8052F143

5. If an external clock or TCXO is used, it should be input via an AC coupling at pin CLK16P with the oscillator powered up and
    AX5043_XTALCAP = 000000. For detailed TCXO network recommendations depending on the TCXO output swing refer to the AX5043
    Application Note: Use with a TCXO Reference Clock.

  The AX8052F143 is a true single chip narrow-band,
ultra-low power RF-microcontroller SoC for use in                  AX8052F143 supports any data rate from 0.1 kbps to
licensed and unlicensed bands ranging from 70 MHz to             125 kbps for FSK, MSK, 4-FSK, GFSK, GMSK and ASK
1050 MHz. The on-chip transceiver consists of a fully            modulations. To achieve optimum performance for specific
integrated RF front-end with modulator and demodulator.          data rates and modulation schemes several register settings
Base band data processing is implemented in an advanced          to configure the AX8052F143 are necessary, they are
and flexible communication controller that enables user          outlined in the following, for details see the AXSEM
friendly communication.                                          RadioLab software which calculates the necessary register
                                                                 settings and the AX5043 Programming Manual.
  The AX8052F143 contains a high speed microcontroller
compatible to the industry standard 8052 instruction set. It       The receiver supports multi-channel operation for all data
contains 64 kBytes of FLASH and 8.25 kBytes of internal          rates and modulation schemes.
SRAM.
                                                                 Microcontroller
  The AX8052F143 features 3 16-bit general purpose                 The AX8052 microcontroller core executes the industry
timers with SD capability, 2 output compare units for
generating PWM signals, 2 input compare units to record          standard 8052 instruction set. Unlike the original 8052,
timings of external signals, 2 16-bit wakeup timers, a           many instructions are executed in a single cycle. The system
watchdog timer, 2 UARTs, a Master/Slave SPI controller, a        clock and thus the instruction rate can be programmed freely
10-bit 500 kSample/s A/D converter, 2 analog comparators,        from DC to 20 MHz.
a temperature sensor, a 2 channel DMA controller, and a
dedicated AES crypto controller. Debugging is aided by a         Memory Architecture
dedicated hardware debug interface controller that connects        The AX8052F143 Microcontroller features the highest
using a 3-wire protocol (1 dedicated wire, 2 shared with
GPIO) to the PC hosting the debug software.                      bandwidth memory architecture of its class. Figure 6 shows
                                                                 the memory architecture. Three bus masters may initiate bus
  While the radio carrier/LO synthesizer can only be             cycles:
clocked by the crystal oscillator (carrier stability
requirements dictate a high stability reference clock in the     · The AX8052 Microcontroller Core
MHz range), the microcontroller and its peripherals provide      · The Direct Memory Access (DMA) Engine
extremely flexible clocking options. The system clock that       · The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) Engine
clocks the microcontroller, as well as peripheral clocks, can
be selected from one of the following clock sources: the         Bus targets include:
crystal oscillator, an internal high speed 20MHz oscillator,
an internal low speed 640 Hz/10 kHz oscillator, or the low       · Two individual 4 kBytes RAM blocks located in X
frequency crystal oscillator. Prescalers offer additional
flexibility with their programmable divide by a power of two        address space, which can be simultaneously accessed
capability. To improve the accuracy of the internal                 and individually shut down or retained during sleep
oscillators, both oscillators may be slaved to the crystal          mode
oscillator.
                                                                 · A 256 Byte RAM located in internal address space,
  AX8052F143 can be operated from a 1.8 V to 3.6 V power
supply over a temperature range of -40°C to 85°C, it                which is always retained during sleep mode
consumes 4 - 51 mA for transmitting, depending on the
output power, 6.8 - 11 mA for receiving.                         · A 64 kBytes FLASH memory located in code space.
                                                                 · Special Function Registers (SFR) located in internal
  The AX8052F143 features make it an ideal interface for
integration into various battery powered solutions such as          address space accessible using direct address mode
ticketing or as transceiver for telemetric applications e.g. in     instructions
sensors. As primary application, the transceiver is intended
for UHF radio equipment in accordance with the European          · Additional Registers located in X address space
Telecommunication Standard Institute (ETSI) specification
EN 300 220-1 and the US Federal Communications                      (X Registers)
Commission (FCC) standard Title 47 CFR part 15 as well as
Part 90. Additionally AX8052F143 is suited for systems             The upper half of the FLASH memory may also be
targeting compliance with Wireless M-Bus standard EN             accessed through the X address space. This simplifies and
13757-4:2005. Wireless M-Bus frame support (S, T, R) is          makes the software more efficient by reducing the need for
built-in.                                                        generic pointers.

  The AX8052F143 sends and receives data in frames. This         NOTE: Generic pointers include, in addition to the
standard operation mode is called Frame Mode. Pre and post                  address, an address space tag.

                                                                   SFR Registers are also accessible through X address
                                                                 space, enabling indirect access to SFR registers. This allows
                                                                 driver code for multiple identical peripherals (such as
                                                                 UARTs or Timers) to be shared.

                                                                   The 4 word × 16 bit fully associative cache and a pre-fetch
                                                                 controller hide the latency of the FLASH.

  The AX8052 Memory Architecture is fully parallel. All         The AES engine accesses memory 16 bits at a time. It is
bus masters may simultaneously access different bus targets   therefore slightly faster to align its buffers on even
during each system clock cycle. Each bus target includes an   addresses.
arbiter that resolves access conflicts. Each arbiter ensures
that no bus master can be starved.                            Memory Map
                                                                The AX8052, like the other industry standard 8052
  Both 4 kBytes RAM blocks may be individually retained
or switched off during sleep mode. The 256 Byte RAM is        compatible microcontrollers, uses a Harvard architecture.
always retained during sleep mode.                            Multiple address spaces are used to access code and data.

  The AX8052 uses P or Code Space to access its program.      AX5043 Programming Manual are relative to the beginning
Code space may also be read using the MOVC instruction.       of RREG, i.e. 0x4000 must be added to these addresses. It
                                                              is recommended that the AXSEM provided ax8052f143.h
  Smaller amounts of data can be placed in the Internal (see  header file is used; Radio Registers are prefixed with
Note) or Data Space. A distinction is made in the upper half  AX5043_ in the ax8052f143.h header file to avoid clashes of
of the Data Space between direct accesses (MOV reg,addr;      same-name Radio Registers with AX8052 registers.
MOV addr,reg) and indirect accesses (MOV reg,@Ri;
MOV @Ri,reg; PUSH; POP); Direct accesses are routed to          Normally, accessing Radio Registers through the RREG
the Special Function Registers, while indirect accesses are   address range is adequate. Since Radio Register accesses
routed to the internal RAM.                                   have a higher latency than other AX8052 registers, the
                                                              AX8052 provides a method for non-blocking access to the
NOTE: The origin of Internal versus External (X) Space        Radio Registers. Accessing the RREG (nb) address range
           is historical. External Space used to be outside   initiates a Radio Register access, but does not wait for its
           of the chip on the original 8052                   completion. The details of mechanism is documented in the
           Microcontrollers.                                  Radio Interface section of the AX8052 Programming
                                                              Manual.
  Large amounts of data can be placed in the External or X
Space. It can be accessed using the MOVX instructions.          The FLASH memory is organized as 64 pages of 1 kBytes
Special Function Registers, as well as additional             each. Each page can be individually erased. The write word
Microcontroller Registers (XREG) and the Radio Registers      size is 16 Bits. The last 1 kByte page is dedicated to factory
(RREG) are also mapped into the X Space.                      calibration data and should not be overwritten.

  Detailed documentation of the Special Function Registers    Power Management
(SFR) and additional Microcontroller Registers can be           The microcontroller power mode can be selected
found in the AX8052 Programming Manual.
                                                              independently from the transceiver. The microcontroller
  The Radio Registers are documented in the AX5043            supports the following power modes:
Programming Manual. Register Addresses given in the

Table 21. POWER MANAGEMENT

 PCON     Name                                                Description
register

00        RUNNING  The microcontroller and all peripherals are running. Current consumption depends on the system clock
                   frequency and the enabled peripherals and their clock frequency.

01        STANDBY  The microcontroller is stopped. All register and memory contents are retained. All peripherals continue to
                   function normally. Current consumption is determined by the enabled peripherals. STANDBY is exited
                   when any of the enabled interrupts become active.

10        SLEEP    The microcontroller and its peripherals, except GPIO and the system controller, are shut down. Their regis-
                   ter settings are lost. The internal RAM is retained. The external RAM is split into two 4 kByte blocks. Soft-
                   ware can determine individually for both blocks whether contents of that block are to be retained or lost.
                   SLEEP can be exited by any of the enabled GPIO or system controller interrupts. For most applications
                   this will be a GPIO or wakeup timer interrupt.

11        DEEPSLEEP The microcontroller, all peripherals and the transceiver are shut down. Only 4 bytes of scratch RAM are

                   retained. DEEPSLEEP can only be exited by tying the PB3 pin low.

                Register                                      Remarks

AX5043_DECIMATION                    This register programs the bandwidth of the digital channel filter.

AX5043_RXDATARATE2... AX5043_RX-     These registers specify the receiver bit rate, relative to the channel filter bandwidth.
DATARATE0

AX5043_MAXDROFFSET2...               These registers specify the maximum possible data rate offset
AX5043_MAXDROFFSET0

AX5043_MAXRFOFFSET2... AX5043_MAXR-  These registers specify the maximum possible RF frequency offset
FOFFSET0

AX5043_TIMEGAIN, AX5043_DRGAIN       These registers specify the aggressiveness of the receiver bit timing recovery. More
                                     aggressive settings allow the receiver to synchronize with shorter preambles, at the
                                     expense of more timing jitter and thus a higher bit error rate at a given signal-to-noise
                                     ratio.

AX5043_MODULATION                    This register selects the modulation to be used by the transmitter and the receiver,
                                     i.e. whether ASK, FSK should be used.

AX5043_PHASEGAIN, AX5043_FREQGAINA,  These registers control the bandwidth of the phase, frequency offset and amplitude
AX5043_FREQGAINB, AX5043_FREQGAINC,  tracking loops.
AX5043_FREQGAIND, AX5043_AMPLGAIN

AX5043_AGCGAIN                       This register controls the AGC (automatic gain control) loop slopes, and thus the
                                     speed of gain adjustments. The faster the bit-rate, the faster the AGC loop should be.

AX5043_TXRATE                        These registers control the bit rate of the transmitter.

AX5043_FSKDEV                        These registers control the frequency deviation of the transmitter in FSK mode. The
                                     receiver does not explicitly need to know the frequency deviation, only the channel
                                     filter bandwidth has to be set wide enough for the complete modulation to pass.

  The encoder is located between the Framing Unit, the          Most radio systems today group data into packets. The

   rate.

Automatic Frequency Control (AFC)                                  PWRMODE Register
  The AX8052F143 features an automatic frequency                     The AX8052F143 transceiver features its own

tracking loop which is capable of tracking the transmitter         independent power management, independent from the
frequency within the RX filter band width. On top of that the      microcontroller. While the microcontroller power mode is
AX8052F143 has a frequency tracking register                       controlled through the PCON register, the
AX5043_TRKRFFREQ to synchronize the receiver                       AX5043_PWRMODE register controls which parts of the
frequency to a carrier signal. For AFC adjustment, the             transceiver are operating.
frequency offset can be computed with the following
formula:

Table 28. PWRMODE REGISTER

AX5043_PWRMODE         Name                                                              Description
        Register
                                     All digital and analog functions, except the register file, are disabled. The core supply volt-
     0000          POWERDOWN         ages are switched off to conserve leakage power. Register contents are preserved.
                                     Access to the FIFO is not possible and the contents are not preserved. POWERDOWN
     0001          DEEPSLEEP         mode is only entered once the FIFO is empty.

     0101              STANDBY       The transceiver is fully turned off. All digital and analog functions are disabled. All register
     0110                 FIFO       contents are lost.
                                     To leave DEEPSLEEP mode the pin SEL has to be pulled low. This will initiate startup and
                                     reset of the transceiver. Then the MISO line should be polled, as it will be held low during
                                     initialization and will rise to high at the end of the initialization, when the chip becomes
                                     ready for operation.
                                     It is recommended to use the functions ax5043_enter_deepsleep() and ax5043_wake-
                                     up_deepsleep() provided in libmf

                                     The crystal oscillator and the reference are powered on; receiver and transmitter are off.
                                     Register contents are preserved and accessible.
                                     Access to the FIFO is not possible and the contents are not preserved. STANDBY is only
                                     entered once the FIFO is empty.

                                     The reference is powered on. Register contents are preserved and accessible.
                                     Access to the FIFO is possible and the contents are preserved.

        Register
                             The synthesizer is running on the receive frequency. Transmitter and receiver are still off.
      1000        SYNTHRX    This mode is used to let the synthesizer settle on the correct frequency for receive.

      1001           FULLRX  Synthesizer and receiver are running.
      1011             WOR
                             Receiver wakeup-on-radio mode.
      1100        SYNTHTX    The mode the same as POWERDOWN, but the 640 Hz internal low power oscillator is
      1101         FULLTX    running.

                             The synthesizer is running on the transmit frequency. Transmitter and receiver are still off.
                             This mode is used to let the synthesizer settle on the correct frequency for transmit.

                             Synthesizer and transmitter are running. Do not switch into this mode before the synthesiz-
                             er has completely settled on the transmit frequency (in SYNTHTX mode), otherwise spuri-
                             ous spectral transmissions will occur.

voltages for the internal circuitry from the primary supply
VDD_IO. The I/O level of the digital pins is VDD_IO.           In power-down mode the core supply voltages for digital

  Pins VDD_ANA are supplied for external decoupling of       power. Most register contents are preserved but access to the
the power supply used for the on-chip PA.                    FIFO is not possible and FIFO contents are lost.

QFN40 Recommended Pad Layout
     1. PCB land and solder masking recommendations
         are shown in Figure 24.

A = Clearance from PCB thermal pad to solder mask opening, 0.0635 mm minimum
B = Clearance from edge of PCB thermal pad to PCB land, 0.2 mm minimum
C = Clearance from PCB land edge to solder mask opening to be as tight as possible

      to ensure that some solder mask remains between PCB pads.
D = PCB land length = QFN solder pad length + 0.1 mm
E = PCB land width = QFN solder pad width + 0.1 mm
